sentences.text: Penelopognathus was a hadrosauroid dinosaur that grew to about 5 meters long and 2 meters tall.
The species Penelopognathus weishampeli was named after David Weishampel and described in 2005 from fragmentary jaw fossils.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of a single straight, elongated jawbone featuring about 20 irregular holes on its outer surface.
Evidence suggests this animal is more derived than Altirhinus but more primitive than Probactrosaurus.
Penelopognathus weishampeli is the only known species of this extinct genus, an ornithopod belonging to the Iguanodontia and the parent group Hadrosauroidea.
It lived during the middle Cretaceous, specifically the Albian stage, approximately 100 million years ago, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian age.
The discovery of Penelopognathus supports the hypothesis that hadrosauroids originated in Asia.
